title: Swiss BACS reports first successful cyberattacks on Swiss companies carried out with AI agents
date_note: Netzwoche's article of 25 November is the earliest page read; the BACS release itself was not found.
geo_basis: country named in the source; no city stated
summary: Netzwoche reports that the Swiss Federal Office for Cybersecurity (BACS) received its first reports of successful cyberattacks on Swiss companies carried out with AI agents; the victims include operators of critical infrastructure. Inside-IT, relaying BACS, says the agents use "Agentic Offensive Frameworks" named Artex and CyberstrikeAI against weak or default passwords and known flaws. BACS expects more fast attacks.
plain: Switzerland's cyber office says it has received its first reports of successful attacks on Swiss companies that used AI agents, including on critical infrastructure operators, and expects more such attacks.
exec: The Swiss cyber office says AI-agent attacks have succeeded against Swiss companies and critical infrastructure operators and expects more fast attacks.
action: BACS advises reducing internet-exposed systems, protecting webmail and VPN with MFA or passkeys, applying least privilege, detecting deviations in behaviour and data volume, and running regular penetration tests.

validation.note: Netzwoche and Inside-IT each report BACS's statement of first successful AI-agent attacks in Switzerland; the BACS release itself was not read. Reports differ on counts (kumparan says four of five attacks succeeded; Inside-IT says every known case compromised the victim; 20min cites five attacks without naming who confirmed them), so no count is given.
